newsitem.title: UK: Minor metals slow, cobalt ponders Zaire situation.
newsitem.headline: Minor metals slow, cobalt ponders Zaire situation.

text.p: Minor metals trading was subdued during a past week which lacked robust consumer business.
Cobalt and antimony continued to drift lower and molybdenum was mauled by further long liquidation.
Prices for cobalt remained unaffected by bloodshed and anarchy in eastern Zaire as the key mining areas are well to the south of the battle zone, traders said.
So far traders have heard of no problems with production at the various facilities in the southern region of Shaba, but they will watch further developments closely.
"It seems that the situation in Zaire could worsen...we could wake up one morning and see cobalt prices two to three dollars higher," one European trader said.
High grade material was last indicated at $21.25/$22.00.
Traders were also focusing on the health of Zairean ruler Mobutu who has recently under gone surgery for prostate cancer.
The Swiss Foreign Ministry has extended Mobutu's visa until Novemeber 27 on medical grounds.
Traders still remained divided over cobalt's next direction.
Several suggested that prices had the potential to move higher near-term against the backdrop of super alloy demand and improving fundamentals.
The bullish end of the market said that Russian production was continuing to decline, while domestic demand was growing.
According to official Japanese figures cobalt imports for the third quarter 1996 were 1,970 tonnes, an increase of 57.5 percent on the same period in 1995.
Downside thinking was centred on the newstream production, which was expected to kick in towards the end of the 1990s.
"Supply is expected to outstrip demand," one trader said.
According to the U.S. Defense National Stockpile Center about 6.1 million lbs of surplus U.S-owned cobalt will be offered for sale during fiscal 1997.
Chinese offers and a lack of consumer demand saw antimony decline further.
"The market is awash with the metal and at present there seems little in the way to stop the decline," one trader said.
Molybdenum moved lower under long liquidation.

Traders said they expected the downside pressure on molybdenum to continue near-term. They explained the drive lower reflected a failure of a recent technical rally and a resumption of Chinese shipments.
